newsitem.title: USA: Walt Disney Q2 broadcasting revs up 9 pct.
newsitem.headline: Walt Disney Q2 broadcasting revs up 9 pct.

text.p: Walt Disney Co said on Wednesday that its broadcasting revenues rose nine percent for the second quarter ended March 31, to $1.5 billion.
Theme park and resort revenues were up 14 percent, to $1.2 billion, while creative-content revenues rose nine percent, to $2.8 billion.

Disney said the broadcasting results benefited from significant reductions in program amortization and other costs attributable to last year's acquisition of ABC, partially offset by lower network ratings.
Cable results, helped by higher advertising revenues and subscribers at ESPN, were a key contributor to the increase in broadcasting revenues.
Disney reported second-quarter net income per share of $0.49 per share, compared with $0.30 on a pro forma basis for the same period the year before.
Creative-content revenues were helped by the performance of such movies as "Ransom" and "101 Dalmations," and by continued growth in worldwide character merchandising.
Theme park and resort revenue growth reflected record attendance levels and increased occupied room nights at Walt Disney World, the company said.
